headline: From bass‑shaking apartments to stray dogs prowling playgrounds, Austin’s 311 complaints this week scream both nightlife chaos and neighborhood anxiety

picks.text: Luna reaching 92 decibels all the way up here on the on 23rd floor
picks.editorialNote: A resident on the 23rd floor measured Luna’s bass at 92 decibels, turning a typical night out into a building‑wide vibration that even reaches shower time. It highlights how outdoor music venues are spilling sound into high‑rise living spaces, blurring the line between entertainment and disturbance.

picks.text: MAKE. LUNA. STOP. PLEASSSSEEEE its the day of the Lord and I can no longer pray in peace
picks.editorialNote: The plea ‘MAKE. LUNA. STOP… it’s the day of the Lord’ captures a desperate plea for peace amid relentless Sunday bass that’s ruining residents’ spiritual routines. This complaint underscores the clash between Austin’s nightlife economy and the everyday sanctity of home life.

picks.text: Luna is causing me to lose my sanity please make them turn it down up
picks.editorialNote: ‘Luna is causing me to lose my sanity please make them turn it down up’ reads like a cry for sanity in a city that never sleeps, showing how repeated loud music can erode mental well‑being. It signals a growing frustration that could pressure officials to enforce stricter noise limits.

picks.text: Loud music is exceeding the allowed noise levels and causing a disturbance. Please investigate and address the violation. Riviere
picks.editorialNote: The complaint that ‘Loud music is exceeding the allowed noise levels… Riviere’ points to a systematic breach of permit limits at a known venue, suggesting gaps in enforcement. It reveals how popular spots can become noise hotspots that affect entire neighborhoods.

picks.text: Whilst I appreciate Mexico won a World Cup game tonight  the drumming and shouting and loud music is deafening and yet again we can not get any rest. I believe it is coming from both The Flower Shop and a bar next door to Cenote on 7th. Please send someone out to sort this out. I am so sorry to be complaining yet again but it is impossible to get any sleep.
picks.editorialNote: A resident laments drumming and shouting ‘deafening’ after Mexico’s World Cup win, pleading for help to restore sleep in a densely packed area. This illustrates how celebratory crowds can quickly become a nightly nuisance for nearby families.

picks.text: Loose aggressive dogs by school. Following me on my walk, lunging and barking and trying to circle me. Originally seen in front of Dobie Middle School. But I've traced these dogs before, and they are from 1113 Crown Oaks Dr. Not sure if their owner lets them out or just won't repair a gap in their yard, but these dogs are not safe.
picks.editorialNote: Three aggressive Rhodesian Ridgebacks have taken over a playground trailhead, lunging at walkers and forcing neighbors to barricade themselves indoors. The report reflects rising concerns about uncontrolled dog packs in public spaces and the need for stronger animal control.

picks.text: Ran up to me and my dogs on our daily walk and attempted to attack my dogs AGAIN. Both then ran into traffic. This is my 3rd report. picks.editorialNote: A dog attacked the reporter’s pets, then charged into traffic, prompting a third 311 call and a near‑miss with a car. This escalation shows how repeated loose‑dog incidents can turn ordinary walks into safety hazards.

picks.editorialNote: An off‑leash dog on the Rainey St trailhead lawn illustrates how simple trail misuse can quickly become a community‑wide nuisance. It signals a broader pattern of pet owners ignoring leash rules in high‑traffic urban corridors.

picks.editorialNote: A yellow off‑leash dog with an irresponsible owner was spotted repeatedly, hinting at a recurring problem that residents can’t ignore. It captures the everyday irritation of encountering uncontrolled pets in shared spaces.
